plan: reports/plans/2026-10-29_plan_reuse-stage1.md (Revision 1): Stage A 'The two checks', 'Bars', 'Rule', 'Possession', A1 table, A2 readings, Predictions PA1-PA4; Stage C 'Pass bar' and Predictions PC1-PC4
units: All accuracies, B, P and probe accuracies are fractions in [0, 1] (the plan's percentages / 100). Table 6 cells in PA2 are in percentage points, as the paper prints them.

definitions.position: `=` (pcfg.ART_POS = 256), the position whose next-token prediction is the answer (pcfg.ANS = 257). Every behaviour read, probe and patch reads or writes here; 'output' = argmax of the logits at `=`.
definitions.prefix: 'C a 40' = Counter family, operand a, window O' = 40 (count over the last 40 text tokens); 'C b 40' likewise for b.
definitions.C_Te_0: fresh Counter sequences with no spurious rows (pcfg.task_batch(..., c_rate=0.0)), drawn from a stream disjoint from training (run.py EVAL_SEED).
definitions.qualifying_input: a C_Te = 0 input with count(b) != count(a) + 1 in the counted window (the plan's 'where count(b) != count(a)+1'), so count-a+1 and count-b outputs differ.
definitions.accuracy_A1: run.py behaviour(): answer_accuracy = share of rows whose argmax at `=` equals the answer token, on 4,000 fresh C_Te = 0 rows of the prior's own operand task, all rows (no qualifying filter; Table 6 also reads plain accuracy). Written to results/a1_<prior>.json (one file per prior) as count_a ('C a 40' rows) and count_b ('C b 40' rows), with iters, eval_n and the behaviour floors.
definitions.behaviour_floors: Measured by run.py a1 on the same 4,000 samples as each accuracy, written to results/a1_<prior>.json: count_a_floor_majority = share of 'C a 40' rows whose answer is the most common answer among those rows (score of always answering the majority label); count_b_floor_majority = the same on 'C b 40' rows; count_b_floor_swap = share of 'C b 40' rows with count(a) == count(b) in the window (score of answering count(a) when asked for count(b)); count_a_mae, count_b_mae = mean |argmax answer - true count| over the rows, in count units. Code review (reports/reviews/2026-10-29_review_e55-code.md, finding 1): window counts take only 9 values (9-17); always answering 13 scores ~35% on count-a; the swap answer scores ~21% on count-b. Accuracies are read against these floors, not against 0.
definitions.B: Behaviour check for an arm and f_C, prefix 'C b 40' (the arm's own task), qualifying inputs only: share of outputs equal to g(f_C(x)), g(count-a) = count_a(x) + 1, g(count-b) = count_b(x). No probe.
definitions.P: Patch check for an arm and f_C: 1,000 pairs (x, x') of qualifying inputs with the same value of the other count and f_C(x') != f_C(x). Replace the residual stream at `=`, output of block l*, in the run on x by the run on x'. P = (number of pairs where patched output == model's output on x' AND model's output on x' != model's output on x) / (number of pairs). Denominator: all pairs built, not conditioned on the model's outputs.
definitions.l_star: l*_a: on LOW, prefix 'C a 40', count-a patch; l*_b: on HIGH, prefix 'C b 40', count-b patch. l* = the earliest of blocks 1..n_layer-1 (1..5; edge_cases.E12) whose positive-control P is >= max over those blocks - 3 s, s = sd of that block's positive-control P over 3 independent sets of 1,000 pairs, floored at the binomial sd at the fewest pairs built over the sets (edge_cases.E14). Fixed in A1 (results/a1c_patch.json a2_bars.l_star_a, l_star_b); every A2 arm uses l*_a for count-a and l*_b for count-b.
definitions.a1c_outputs: run.py a1c-patch -> results/a1c_patch.json: patch (P per set and block for the four P references, n_pairs_a, n_pairs_b), behaviour_nulls (B_a_null, B_b_null per set), a2_bars (l_star_a, l_star_b and the four bars B_a, P_a, B_b, P_b, each n0, s, p_plus, lo, hi, void), PA1_rows (the five behaviour cells and the patch and B-null rows), stops. run.py a1c-probe -> results/a1c_probe.json: probes (raw, margins, m_plus, possessed), PA1_rows (the three probe rows), PA4_LOW_possesses_count_b, stops. The A2 bars are filed by copying a1c_patch.json's a2_bars into this file's a2_bars, dated; run.py a2 refuses to start (exit 2) until then and checks that the filed l* equal a1c_patch.json's.

references.P_a_positive: count-a patch on LOW, prefix 'C a 40', block l*_a
references.P_b_positive: count-b patch on HIGH, prefix 'C b 40', block l*_b
references.P_a_null: count-a patch on NEVER, prefix 'C b 40' (NEVER counts b, never counted a), block l*_a
references.P_b_null: count-b patch on LOW, prefix 'C a 40', block l*_b
references.B_a_null: B for count-a (outputs == count_a + 1) on NEVER, prefix 'C b 40', qualifying inputs
references.B_b_null: B for count-b (outputs == count_b) on LOW, prefix 'C b 40', qualifying inputs (edge_cases.E1; not stated in the plan)

definitions.probe: linear, vocabulary-sized softmax on the residual at `=`, output of each block; 4K AdamW iterations, lr 1e-3, x0.1 at 2K, 3K, 3.5K; fresh C_Te = 0 samples per batch; accuracy on 2,000 held-out samples. Target f_C: count-a on 'C a 40', count-b on 'C b 40'. Controls: the shuffled-label probe on the same model and block; for count-a also NEVER's count-a probe at the same block. Majority-class rate reported beside each accuracy.
definitions.margin: m(model, f_C, block) = probe accuracy - max(control accuracies at that block); s = sd of m over 3 probe seeds at that block (floored, edge_cases.E3). m_plus = LOW's count-a margin at its best block (argmax m), with s_plus its s.
definitions.possession: Possessed iff at some block m >= 3 s and m >= 0.5 x m_plus. Void (no reading) iff m_plus < 6 s_plus (see edge_cases.E4).

bar_rule.rule: For each of the four checks (B_a, P_a, B_b, P_b): n0 = null reference mean over 3 independent sample sets; p_plus = positive reference; s = max(sd of the null over the 3 sets, binomial sd sqrt(n0 (1 - n0) / n)), floored per edge_cases.E2, n = the samples the null reads (B: 1,000 qualifying inputs; P: the fewest pairs built over the 3 sets, >= 500; edge_cases.E14). lo = n0 + max(3 s, 0.1 (p_plus - n0)) (edge_cases.E13); hi = n0 + 0.5 (p_plus - n0). If hi <= lo the check is void for the whole stage: stop (apparatus).
bar_rule.relative_or_absolute: lo and hi are absolute fractions computed from measured references (relative to n0 and p_plus); once filed they are fixed numbers.
bar_rule.label_rule: An arm state 'goes through f_C' iff B > hi_B and P > hi_P; 'does not go through f_C' iff B < lo_B and P < lo_P; else 'neither'. Strict inequalities because the plan files 'ties at a bar count as neither' (edge_cases.E5). A check whose reference failed is void for that arm (edge_cases.E7), and an arm with a void check reads 'neither'. Fewer than 500 qualifying pairs for P -> P void -> 'neither'.

a2_bars.filed: 2026-10-29 (fourth filing), copied unchanged from results/a1c_patch.json a2_bars (commit 55da119, jobs 44306 44307) by the rule in bar_rule, before any run of a2

PA1.claim: A1 (pretrained LOW, HIGH, NEVER, before any fine-tune) reads as tabled in the plan's A1 table.
PA1.lean: high for the behaviour rows (Table 6: LOW 99.9 / 5.2, HIGH 99.8 / 99.7); medium for the probe-margin and patch rows (no prior patching on PCFG).

behaviour.measurement: results/a1_<prior>.json, written by run.py a1: count_a and count_b, n = eval_n = 4000 fresh C_Te = 0 rows per number, all rows, argmax at `=`. Scored only if iters == 50000 and eval_n == 4000. Reported beside each accuracy, same samples (definitions.behaviour_floors): count_a_floor_majority, count_b_floor_majority, count_b_floor_swap, count_a_mae, count_b_mae.

thresholds.LOW.count_b: <= count_b_floor_swap + 0.10 (LOW's own swap floor on the same 4,000 samples; replaces the plan's <= 0.20, edge_cases.E11)

behaviour.stop: any of the five thresholded cells misses -> stop (recipe); numbers to the user (Blocking card); no bars filed, no A2.
behaviour.noise_floor: binomial sd at n = 4000: 0.0034 at 0.95, 0.0063 at 0.20; the bands are > 10 sd from Table 6's values.

count_a_probe_margin.measurement: m at the best block (argmax m over blocks), count-a probe on 'C a 40'; controls shuffled-label and NEVER's count-a probe. Read from results/a1c_probe.json (definitions.a1c_outputs).

thresholds.NEVER: a control (its accuracy enters LOW's and HIGH's max(controls)); no threshold

count_a_probe_margin.relative_or_absolute: LOW: relative to its own s; HIGH: relative to m_plus
count_a_probe_margin.stop: m_plus < 6 s_plus -> stop (probe). HIGH < 0.5 m_plus: the plan names no stop for this cell; it is a PA1 miss, reported (see ambiguities_resolved).

count_b_probe_margin.measurement: m at the best block, count-b probe on 'C b 40'; control shuffled-label only. Read from results/a1c_probe.json.

patch_positive.measurement: P_a_positive at l*_a (LOW, 'C a 40'), P_b_positive at l*_b (HIGH, 'C b 40'); 1,000 pairs, 3 independent sets, mean. Read from results/a1c_patch.json.
patch_positive.stop: hi <= lo for the check it references (bar_rule) -> stop. A value under 0.8 with hi > lo is a PA1 miss, reported, not a stop.

patch_and_behaviour_null.measurement: P_a_null (NEVER, 'C b 40', l*_a), B_a_null (NEVER, 'C b 40'), P_b_null (LOW, 'C a 40', l*_b); 3 independent sets each, mean. Read from results/a1c_patch.json.
patch_and_behaviour_null.stop: hi <= lo for the check it references -> stop. A value over 0.05 with hi > lo is a PA1 miss, reported, not a stop.

PA1.blind_to: Behaviour: plain accuracy on the own task, not whether count-a is the route. Probe margin: linear decodability at `=`, not use. Patch positive controls: that the patched block carries the count on the model's own task, not on another task's prefix.
PA1.positive_control: LOW's count-a (behaviour 99.9% in Table 6; probe m_plus; P_a_positive) and HIGH's count-b.
PA1.noise_floor: behaviour: binomial at 4,000; probe: s over 3 probe seeds; patch: sd over 3 sets of 1,000 pairs, floored at the binomial sd (edge_cases.E2).

PA2.claim: The fine-tunes reproduce Table 6: count-b accuracy on C_Te = 0 at 10K iterations is within 15 points of Table 6 in >= 7 of the 9 10K cells.
PA2.measurement: answer_accuracy of the arm's 10K state on fresh C_Te = 0 'C b 40' rows, all rows (as Table 6 and A1), argmax at `=`, x100. n = 4,000 (A1's eval_n; the plan does not state A2's n, see ambiguities_resolved). FT seed 0 for every arm.
PA2.threshold: cell within iff |acc_percent - Table6_percent| <= 15 (absolute points, inclusive); PA2 holds iff >= 7 of 9 cells within.
PA2.role: Reported, not a gate: labels come from the checks.
PA2.label_spread_note: Our window counts are 13 +- 1 (code review finding 2: every d/e/f leaf holds roughly one of each of a, b, c), while Jain's Fig. 16 calls theirs 'fairly spread' on a 0-40 axis. The Table 6 cells may therefore sit on a different floor from ours (majority and swap floors, definitions.behaviour_floors); a PA2 miss or pass is read with that in mind, and PA2 stays reported, not a gate.
PA2.count_a_plus_1_floor_note: Filed 2026-10-29 before a2 (code review risk 5): a W that keeps answering count(a) + 1 scores P(count_b = count_a + 1) on natural C_Te = 0 rows, measured ~0.188 by the reviewer, while Table 6 prints W1 0 and W2 1.9; so both W cells can sit more than 15 points off by construction and PA2 can reach at most 7 of 9. Each a2 state's count_b_te0 row carries floor_count_a_plus_1 (that share on the same 4,000 rows; run.py a1 writes count_b_floor_count_a_plus_1 too, but the a1_<prior>.json files predate it), and the W1 and W2 cells are read beside it. PA2's rule and threshold are unchanged.
PA2.blind_to: Which route the accuracy uses; 1K states; the C_Te = 1 column.
PA2.positive_control: A1's behaviour rows (same accuracy code, LOW and HIGH bases against Table 6).
PA2.noise_floor: binomial sd at 4,000 <= 0.8 points; FT seed noise from the second seeds of W1 and N1, reported, not used.

PA3.claim: W1 and W2 read 'through count-a' at both states (1K, 10K); N1 reads 'not through count-a' at both states; R reads 'through count-b'.
PA3.measurement: label_rule on B and P at `=` for each state, with the A2 bars filed from A1: count-a checks (B_a, P_a at l*_a) for W1, W2, N1; count-b checks (B_b, P_b at l*_b) for R. B on qualifying 'C b 40' inputs; P on 1,000 pairs. R is read at its 10K state (the plan counts R as one state; see ambiguities_resolved).
PA3.thresholds: lo, hi per check from a2_bars (not yet filed).
PA3.relative_or_absolute: absolute once filed (derived from A1 references)
PA3.holds_iff: all 7 readings as stated (W1 1K, W1 10K, W2 1K, W2 10K: through count-a; N1 1K, N1 10K: not through count-a; R: through count-b). Any 'neither' or void is a miss.
PA3.reversal: W1 or W2 reads 'not through count-a', or N1 reads 'through count-a' -> filed prediction reversed: stop and tell the user (decision tree 3). B and P disagree (one above hi, the other below lo) on >= 3 of the 17 states -> the null: card to the user, no scoring.
PA3.lean: medium: W's output on C_Te = 0 is unknown (Table 6 says only that it is not count_b); W could read 'neither'.
PA3.blind_to: A W that computes count-a after l* from text positions (P low, B high -> 'neither'); a shared counter re-bound to a new operand reads 'not through count-a' and is reported as such. Spurious-row artifacts of the a<->c swaps (pcfg.py; code review 2026-10-29 risk 4, kept because Jain's construction also inserts tokens artificially): (i) on every spurious row count_a + count_b + count_c = 40 and count_b = count_a + 1, so the label equals (41 - count_c) / 2; a W that learned 'through count-c' and one that learned 'through count-a' both fit the training rows, and a donor matched on count(b) cannot tell them apart, since changing count(a) at fixed count(b) changes count(c) too; such a W reads 'neither' on qualifying natural inputs, not 'through count-a'. (ii) the swaps leave a 'ccc' trigram at 0.95% of window positions in spurious rows (never in natural text; 'cc' rises 0.050 -> 0.079, mean count(c) +1), so mixed arms (N2, N3, M2, M3) can tell row types apart and learn a row-type switch. Measured by the reviewer on 20K natural and 20K spurious texts; not re-measured by a2.
PA3.positive_control: P_a_positive and P_b_positive in A1; R within A2 for count-b.
PA3.noise_floor: s of each check (bar_rule); FT seed noise from W1 and N1 second seeds, reported, not used for bars.

PA4.claim: LOW possesses count-b (Def 1): its count-b probe at `=` on 'C b 40' clears the possession rule at some block.
PA4.measurement: possession rule (definitions.possession) on LOW, f_C = count-b, controls = shuffled-label probe, s over 3 probe seeds; held-out n = 2,000; majority-class rate reported.
PA4.thresholds: m >= 3 s and m >= 0.5 x m_plus at some block
PA4.lean: 50%: count-b output is 5%, but every family counts tokens, and Jain's Fig. 8 shows readouts outliving behaviour.
PA4.consequence: N1 is 'new' iff PA4 fails; if it holds, N1 reuses a count-b readout LOW had but did not output.
PA4.blind_to: Use: a decodable count is not one the model computes with; 'at some block' over all blocks inflates false positives slightly.
PA4.noise_floor: s over 3 probe seeds (floored, edge_cases.E3). FT seed noise (two seeds of W1 and N1) is reported, not used for bars.
PA4.void: m_plus < 6 s_plus, or m_plus <= 0 (edge_cases.E4) -> PA4 unscored (and A1 stops, PA1).

stage_C.pass_bar: a = smallest count with P(Binomial(n, 0.5) >= a) <= 0.05, raised to (majority truth-class count + 1) if higher. Instrument passes iff agreements >= a. n = labelled LOW states ('neither' excluded) not voided for that instrument; + R for steering only. Truth 'through count-a' (R: 'through count-b') = existing.

predictions.PC1_pruning_passes: lean low (Fig. 76/77: revival at every C_Tr after a 1e-4 FT)
predictions.PC2_reverse_ft_passes: lean low (Fig. 9: LOW revives at ~3K, near scratch)
predictions.PC4_vpd_r_passes: lean low-medium; gated, runs only after the user's go-ahead

stage_C.instrument_rules: As the plan states (Stage C, C1/C2); each is blind to 'neither' arms. A failed instrument baseline voids that arm for that instrument (n shrinks), never a vote.
stage_C.fewer_than_8: Fewer than 8 labelled states -> C1 reported without pass bars; C2 not proposed (decision tree 3).

edge_cases.E1_B_b_null_missing: INCOMPLETE in the plan: the A1 references give no null for B on count-b (only the count-b patch null). Without it B_b's lo/hi, and so R's PA3 reading, cannot be computed. Filed: B_b null = B for count-b (outputs == count_b) on LOW, prefix 'C b 40', qualifying inputs (the arms' base on the arms' task; Table 6 puts it near 0.05).
edge_cases.E2_zero_spread: DEGENERATE: a null of exactly 0 with identical sets gives s = 0 (binomial sd sqrt(0) = 0), so lo = 0 and, with ties as 'neither', 'not through' becomes impossible. Filed: the binomial sd uses n0 clipped to [1/1000, 1 - 1/1000], so s >= sqrt(0.001 x 0.999 / 1000) = 0.0010 and lo >= n0 + 0.0030.
edge_cases.E3_probe_zero_spread: DEGENERATE: three probe seeds with identical accuracies give s = 0, so 'm >= 3 s' is met by any m >= 0. Filed: s floored at the binomial sd of the held-out accuracy at n = 2,000, accuracy clipped to [1/2000, 1 - 1/2000].
edge_cases.E4_m_plus_zero: DEGENERATE: m_plus = 0 with s_plus = 0 gives 'm_plus < 6 s_plus' false (not void) and then every m >= 0 is possessed. With E3's floor s_plus > 0, so m_plus = 0 is void. Also m_plus <= 0 is void outright; a tie m_plus = 6 s_plus is not void (the plan's strict '<').
edge_cases.E5_ties: The plan's rule says B >= hi and B <= lo but files 'ties at a bar count as neither'. Read as strict inequalities (the specific clause wins): B == hi or P == lo etc. -> 'neither'. In A1 rows (PA1 thresholds) ties pass (inclusive), as the plan writes them with >= and <=.
edge_cases.E6_empty_pools: Zero qualifying inputs for B, or zero pairs for P -> that check is void for the state (never 0 or a pass); < 500 qualifying pairs -> P void (plan). A missing results/a1_<prior>.json, iters != 50000, eval_n != 4000, or a non-finite value -> ERROR, never a pass; a NaN fails every threshold it enters. PA2: a missing or non-finite 10K cell counts as outside, denominator stays 9.
edge_cases.E7_void_scope: 'A check whose reference failed is void for that arm': read as a reference that hit its A1 stop column (behaviour cell miss, hi <= lo) - which stops the stage anyway. A PA1 expected-value miss (positive P < 0.8 or null > 0.05 with hi > lo) is reported and does not void.
edge_cases.E8_l_star_ties: Several blocks within 3 s of the max -> the earliest (plan). s = 0 -> l* = earliest block attaining the max (E2's floor applies to s here too).
edge_cases.E9_stage_C_degenerate: n <= 4: no a with P <= 0.05 exists (0.5^n > 0.05) -> instrument unscorable (already covered by 'fewer than 8 -> no pass bars'). All labelled states in one truth class: the majority raise sets a = n + 1, so even a perfect labeller fails; filed: scoring void, agreement reported.
edge_cases.E10_hi_le_lo: p_plus <= n0 gives hi <= n0 < lo -> void (stop), covered by the plan's hi <= lo rule.
edge_cases.E11_LOW_count_b_vs_swap_floor: DEGENERATE (code review, 2026-10-29): the plan's LOW count-b stop '<= 0.20' sits under the ~21% that answering count(a) when asked for count(b) scores, so a LOW that simply answers its count-a on 'C b 40' (the expected behaviour, Table 6: 5.2%) could miss the row by the floor alone, or a stop could fire with no recipe fault. Fix (coordinator): LOW.count_b <= count_b_floor_swap + 0.10, the floor measured on the same 4,000 samples (absolute, inclusive). Filed before any A1 run.
edge_cases.E12_l_star_last_block: DEGENERATE (code review 2026-10-29, risk 2): patching the residual at `=` after the last block (6) sets the output to the donor's, so P(6) = share(donor output != own output), ~1 on any accurate model; the max over blocks is then trivially at block 6, l* lands there whenever no earlier block carries the count within 3 s of ~1, and P at l* measures only that the output depends on f_C, the same thing B measures (the two checks collapse into one). Filed: l* candidates are blocks 1..n_layer-1 (1..5); the max and the 3 s window are taken over those blocks only. P at block 6 is still computed and reported (P_by_block). Filed before any a1c run.
edge_cases.E13_bar_lo_zero_null: DEGENERATE (code review 2026-10-29, risk 3): a null of exactly 0 (e.g. B_a on NEVER, which never answers count_a + 1 on qualifying inputs) gives s at E2's floor and lo = 0.0030, so an N state with ~1% off-by-one answers (counts sit in 9-17, so a +-1 error often lands on count_a + 1) reads 'neither' for a trivial reason, a PA3 miss that is not a reuse finding. Filed: lo = n0 + max(3 s, 0.1 (p_plus - n0)); hi unchanged (n0 + 0.5 (p_plus - n0)); void iff hi <= lo as before. Since 0.1 < 0.5, the new term alone never voids a bar. Filed before any a1c run.
edge_cases.E14_binomial_n: The binomial sd floor (E2, used by l* and the bars) was computed at a fixed n = 1,000, while P may rest on 500-999 pairs. Filed: n = the samples actually read: for B, the 1,000 qualifying inputs; for P (the P bars and l*), the fewest pairs built over the 3 sets (>= 500, else P is void, E6). Filed before any a1c run.

ambiguities_resolved: Block indexing for l* and the probes: whether the embedding output (before block 1) is a candidate; filed: block outputs 1..6 (the embedding output is not a candidate).
n for B in A2 is not stated; the bar's binomial sd assumes 1,000. Filed: B on the first 1,000 qualifying inputs of the evaluation stream.
R is one state ('16 LOW states + R', '17 states'); filed as R's 10K state.
HIGH's count-a probe margin row has no stop in the plan; filed as a reported PA1 miss.

run.py a1 writes only behaviour and its floors (results/a1_<prior>.json); the probe and patch numbers and the B nulls need A1 code not yet written (run.py's comment at line 147 still names the pre-revision rows: count-c selectivity, ablation). Their output fields are to be named when that code is written.
The plan's context length is 262; pcfg.py's SEQ is 259 (ANS = 257, 2 after). Not a prediction issue; noted.
not_run: Edge cases were worked by hand against the rules above (no code yet implements the bars, probe or patch); the Stage C binomial values were checked by hand.
